intro.text: The wife of Highprince Torol Sadeas, who uses Dalinar's recruitment drive to plant more spies in his warcamp.
An Alethi lighteyed noblewoman and the wife of Highprince Torol Sadeas, living in his warcamp on the Shattered Plains.
The widow of Highprince Torol Sadeas, who has moved to Urithiru with the rest of the Alethi.
The widow of Highprince Torol Sadeas, who has made Meridas Amaram highprince of House Sadeas and works against Dalinar Kholin's coalition.
The widow of Torol Sadeas, who left Urithiru in disgrace and took charge of the Sons of Honor in the warcamps on the Shattered Plains.

items.text: Ialai married Torol Sadeas before the unification of Alethkar and threw herself into Alethi politics. At a feast in 1143 she urged Dalinar Kholin to make a political match with Evi, though she thought Evi vapid, and afterwards she and Navani pressed Evi to be more assertive. With their husbands often at war, Ialai and Navani worked together in Kholinar to keep the kingdom stable, and King Gavilar happily used Ialai's schemes against his rivals.
Ialai was present when Torol won a King's Boon from Gavilar and then defeated Yenev in a duel.
During the War of Reckoning, Ialai lived in the Sadeas warcamp. When Shallan Davar arrived with news of Jasnah's presumed death, Ialai haughtily asked her about the succession in Jah Keved.

Ialai and Torol plotted against the other highprinces and curried favour with Elhokar while defying the throne's authority, often targeting Dalinar and Adolin. Unsettled when Dalinar nearly set up a duel between Adolin and Torol, they vowed to destroy Dalinar by any means.

Through her spies, Ialai obtained Navani's notes on Dalinar's visions, altered them to discredit him, and released them at a feast, but Dalinar embraced their publication. A carpenter in the Sadeases' employ then collapsed a bridge under Dalinar; when he survived, Ialai felt she had failed.

Ialai and Torol considered a coup, but decided Dalinar would probably die in his assault on the Parshendi. They did not foresee Aladar siding with Dalinar, whose added army let the Alethi hold out at the Battle of Narak until the Oathgate to Urithiru was opened.

Ialai moved to Urithiru, where Torol was murdered a few days after they arrived. Genuinely upset, she blamed someone in the Kholin army, lashed out at Adolin when he questioned her, and had Meridas Amaram investigate, though she did not think Dalinar himself was the killer. She threatened to return to the warcamps, but had no intention of leaving the seat of power.
Meanwhile the Ghostbloods were watching Ialai closely, and Mraize himself posed as a Sadeas soldier to get near her.

Ialai stopped openly opposing Dalinar, which only worried him, and named Amaram the new Highprince of House Sadeas as an affront to his authority. At a meeting of the coalition of monarchs she refused to carry her own chair, proposed invading Shinovar and insulted Queen Fen; at a later one, her sparring with Jasnah helped Dalinar realise the enemy would strike Thaylen City.
Amaram and the Sadeas army joined Odium's forces at the Battle of Thaylen Field and were defeated. Amaram was killed, and Ialai left Urithiru in disgrace.

Back in the warcamps, Ialai was left in control of the local economy after Thanadal was assassinated and Vamah fled, and others assumed she was behind Thanadal's death. She became leader of the Sons of Honor, though she could do little for them, and kept a cult-like following who called her the true queen of Alethkar. Shallan infiltrated her group disguised as a merchant, Chanasha Hasareh, and was led to the fortress where Ialai was hiding.

Frail and paranoid, Ialai took Shallan for a Ghostblood agent. She said the Ghostbloods had killed Thanadal and Vamah and were wiping out the Sons of Honor for what they knew, and that she believed Gavinor, not herself, the rightful ruler. As she was taken into custody she died of poison, officially by her own hand. At her hint, Shallan searched her quarters and found notes on her attempts to contact Restares and on Shadesmar and other worlds.
Shallan suspected a spy among her team had poisoned Ialai, but could not find one. She later regained her memories of killing Ialai herself.

appearance.text: Ialai is short, squat and curvaceous, with a slender neck, a wide mouth with thick lips, and green eyes. Her hair is black, though she reportedly has some foreign ancestry and dyes it to look fully Alethi. She dresses in the latest Alethi fashions, and after a series of stressful events she grows gaunt and haggard.

personality.text: Ialai has been underhanded since her youth, always sizing up people and situations for weaknesses to exploit. Jasnah thinks her as shrewd as her husband, and Mraize considers the pair so self-serving as to be wholly unpredictable.

Torol was drawn to Ialai's blasphemous name and her dangerous personality. The two are like-minded partners who share news of Alethi politics and scheme together for wealth and influence, with little regard for anyone else.
She runs the best network of spies and informants in the warcamps, including assassins, and keeps it a closely guarded secret.
In public she is a perfect Alethi lady, but in private she likes to lounge. She knows her wine and enjoys food normally served to men.
